from.place: The term-lifting hypothesis in the finite stably free specialization of the general lifting lemma.

title: Lifting a finite stably free module modulo a Jacobson ideal
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and I an ideal such that every element of 1+I is a unit. Let E be a finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] stably free R/I-module, meaning E × F is free for some finite free module F [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then there is a finite stably free R-module P and an R/I-linear isomorphism E ≃ (R/I) ⊗_R P.

proof.text: Choose a finite free complement F such that E × F is finite free. Use bases to construct finite free R-modules A and B reducing to E × F and F. Projectivity of A lifts the reduced projection to a linear map f : A → B, by lifting through the surjective quotient-tensor map B → (R/I) ⊗ B. Tensor extensionality identifies its reduced map with the prescribed projection.

The reduced projection is surjective, so surjectivity detection makes f surjective. Since B is free, it is projective and supplies a section g. Construct P=ker(f) and the map A → P sending x to x-g(f(x)). It retracts the inclusion. The explicit bijection P × B → A, (p,b) ↦ p+g(b), makes P finite stably free.

The retraction remains a retraction after base change, hence the reduced inclusion u : (R/I) ⊗ P → (R/I) ⊗ A is injective. Mathlib lTensor_exact, applied to the exact kernel sequence and the surjection f, identifies its image with the kernel of the reduced projection. Under (R/I) ⊗ A ≃ E × F this kernel is E × 0. Projection to E is therefore bijective on (R/I) ⊗ P and gives the claimed isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_stablyFree_lift
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (hunits : ∀ x : I, IsUnit (1 + (x : R)))
    (E : ModuleCat.{max u v} (R ⧸ I))
    [Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) E] [Module.IsStablyFree (R ⧸ I) E] :
    ∃ P : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
      (Module.Finite R P ∧ Module.IsStablyFree R P) ∧
      Nonempty (E ≅ (ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj P)
